sections.h2: What should a Voorhees homeowner know before selling fast?
sections.html:
Selling fast in Voorhees depends on three things: whether the township will sign off on the house, how much the state collects at closing, and how soon a buyer can fund. Voorhees Township is a Camden County suburb of Philadelphia, with a mix of detached houses, townhouses and apartments.

Owners usually weigh a regular listing, a sale without an agent, and a buyer who pays cash and takes the house with its flaws. All three meet the same township and state steps. The difference is how long you carry the house and how much you spend on repairs first.

sections.h2: Where is Voorhees and what shapes its housing market?
sections.html:
Voorhees covers 11.47 square miles of land in western Camden County and was incorporated in 1899 out of Waterford Township. Census counts jumped from 1,450 in 1940 to 12,919 in 1980 and 24,559 in 1990, which is when most of the housing stock went up. The 2020 census counted 31,069 residents, and the Census Bureau estimates 31,571 for July 1, 2025.

The township borders Cherry Hill, Gibbsboro, Berlin Township, Lindenwold, Somerdale and Lawnside in Camden County, plus Evesham Township in Burlington County. Echelon, the census-designated place in the western part of town, held 11,896 people in 2020. Older names such as Kresson, Kirkwood, Glendale and Osage still show up in addresses and school names.

  • Route 73 (Berlin-Kresson Road) is the only major highway that runs through Voorhees.
  • Interstate 295 and Route 70 reach Philadelphia by way of Cherry Hill, and Exit 32 of I-295 is partly signed for Voorhees.
  • The Ashland station of the PATCO Speedline sits inside the township, and NJ Transit runs the 403 bus to Philadelphia.

Virtua Voorhees Hospital on Route 73 opened in May 2011 on a 40-acre site. The township offices sit at Voorhees Town Center, the former Echelon Mall. New Jersey American Water, the state's largest water utility, was long headquartered here, and the Flyers Training Center draws professional hockey players to the area.

Only 62.0% of homes are owner-occupied, which is low for a New Jersey suburb and points to a sizable stock of condominiums, townhouses and rentals next to the detached houses. If you own a townhouse or condo, ask your association what documents it issues for a sale.

Voorhees Township Public Schools teach pre-kindergarten through eighth grade. The district listed five schools in the 2019-20 school year: Hamilton, Kresson, Osage and Signal Hill elementary schools, and Voorhees Middle School with 1,018 students. High school students attend Eastern Camden County Regional High School, which the township shares with Berlin Borough and Gibbsboro.

Edward T. Hamilton Elementary was named a National Blue Ribbon School in 2003-2004. The Camden County Library's largest branch, the M. Allan Vogelson Regional Branch, is in Voorhees. Voorhees has four elementary schools, so find out which one your street feeds before you list.

sections.h2: What does the township require before a Voorhees house changes hands?
sections.html:
Voorhees runs its resale approval through the township construction office, which handles certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy. Ask that office whether your sale needs a resale certificate, what inspection comes with it, and how long the certificate stays valid before closing.

Unpermitted work is the usual snag. A finished basement, a deck or a converted garage built without a permit can hold up the certificate until the owner closes the permit or removes the work. Pull your permit history early and ask about open items before a contract is signed.

  • State rule for one- and two-family homes: smoke alarms with 10-year sealed batteries must be in place before a sale or change of occupancy (N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19).
  • The state rule does not apply to hardwired or low-voltage alarm systems or to carbon monoxide alarms.
  • Ask the construction office for the current checklist, inspection fee and scheduling window.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when you sell in Voorhees?
sections.html:
At closing the seller pays the state's Realty Transfer Fee, a charge set per $500 of price by bracket. On the state chart for sales over $350,000, the bracket from $200,000 to $550,000 is $4.80 per $500, and that bracket holds the Census median of $429,700 for Voorhees homes. Prices over $1 million bring an extra 1% charge to the buyer and a graduated fee to the seller.

Each owner on the deed signs a GIT/REP form. A seller who still lives in New Jersey signs GIT/REP-3 and prepays nothing, while someone relocating elsewhere may have to send the state 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain. A main home owned and used for two of the five years before closing can shelter part or all of the gain from federal tax.

Ask your closing attorney to send the transfer fee affidavit and the GIT/REP form in with the deed, since the county clerk can refuse a deed that arrives short.

sections.h2: How do property tax assessments and appeals work in Voorhees?
sections.html:
An owner who disputes a Voorhees assessment files with the Camden County Board of Taxation, 509 Lakeland Road in Blackwood, phone 856-225-5238. Camden County keeps the regular calendar, so the filing date is April 1, moving to May 1 after a municipal revaluation. A property valued above $1,000,000 can skip the county board and go to Tax Court.

The board weighs comparable sales more than your opinion of fair value. An appeal does little for a seller about to close, though a buyer or heir who keeps the house might benefit. Owners of a main home may qualify for the state's Homestead Benefit or Senior Freeze, and the township itself handles local deductions for seniors, disabled owners and veterans. Ask the Voorhees tax assessor which ones are on your account.

sections.h2: What are your options for a quick sale in Voorhees?
sections.html:
Which route fits depends on how the house looks and how soon you must close.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure, though showings, repairs, the resale certificate and a lender's schedule add weeks.
  • Sale without an agent: you keep the commission and take on pricing, contracts and township paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: no underwriting or appraisal, and closings in a few weeks are common when the buyer accepts the house in its current state.

Inherited houses, homes with tenants and houses with deferred repairs gain the most from a cash sale. Compare what you keep after fees on each path, not the headline price.

faqs.q: How soon could a Voorhees house sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale often closes within a few weeks. A listed sale runs longer because of showings, the buyer's loan and any township review. Ask the construction office how long its resale inspection takes.

faqs.q: Does Voorhees need an occupancy certificate for a sale?
faqs.a: Ask the township construction office, which issues certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy for a change of owner. Separately, state law calls for 10-year sealed-battery smoke alarms in one- and two-family homes before a sale.

faqs.q: Who covers the New Jersey transfer fee on a Voorhees sale?
faqs.a: The seller. It is collected when the deed is recorded. Buyers owe a separate 1% only at $1 million or above, well over Voorhees's $429,700 Census median home value.

faqs.q: What is the last day to contest a Voorhees assessment?
faqs.a: April 1 for Camden County, or May 1 after a revaluation. Use Form A-1 with the Camden County Board of Taxation in Blackwood at 856-225-5238.

faqs.q: Will open permits stop me from selling in Voorhees?
faqs.a: They can slow the township's sign-off. Ask the construction office to review your permit history, then close the permits or agree in writing with the buyer on who repairs what and by when.
